# Pictures, lettering, reliefs, threads

The person can paste, drop or attach pictures (and PDF drawings) in the panel; you see them, and the files sit in your folder (`attachments/…`, listed in the message). For a part to use one, `./ise image add attachments/<file>` and use the id it prints. Compare your work against a reference with `./ise look`.

- `relief(img, { width, depth, base, mode })`: brightness becomes height; "emboss" (a plaque, light stands high), "engrave" (a cutter, dark cuts deep), "lithophane" (thin where light). `border`, `smooth`, `gamma`, `invert`. Watertight, fast, follows the picture within `tolerance`.
- A round object from a photo or drawing (a vase, a bottle, a lamp base): `./ise image profile attachments/<file> --height <real height mm>` measures its silhouette against the background and prints the profile as `[radius, z]` points, bottom up, plus how far the outline's middle strays (perspective, tilt); a shadow beside the foot is left out, and it says when the top is a rim seen from a little above (`--rim` measures from the rim's line). In a program `image(id).profile({ height, rows, rim })` gives the same `points` and a closed `outline` live from the picture (`image(id).silhouette({ rows })` the pixels): revolve it, or run a `spline` through the points for a smooth wall, then shell it. Look at the photo too: the measured outline includes a lip, foot or shadow the photo shows; trim what is not the object.
- `trace(img, { width, threshold, invert })`: a logo or line drawing as a Profile (extrude, emboss, engrave, cut through); `profile.loops` gives the points (a silhouette's half to revolve); `channel: "object"` traces what stands out from a photo's backdrop (an object on white) rather than what is dark. `image(id).grid(nx)` reads pixel values to measure a picture yourself. Photos of an object to model in 3D go on canvases instead: see the next section.
- `text(str, { size, weight, align, valign, arc })`: real font outlines (Inter built in; a stored font by id). `graduations({ length | radius, step, every })` for scales and dials.
- `part.emboss(decor, { at, normal, height })`, `part.engrave(decor, { at, normal, depth })`, or `{ cylinder: { radius, angle, z } }` to wrap onto a cylinder; `solid.wrap(radius)` and `placeOn(solid, { at, normal })` for your own.
- A printed label, decal or pad-printed artwork (a battery's wrap label, a rating plate sticker, a logo printed on a housing): a thin part in the label's outline (0.05–0.1 mm, lying on the face) whose material names the picture, e.g. `Label print battery-label.png` (the name it was added with by `./ise image add` — give an attachment a readable one with `--name battery-label.png` — or its id, or the id's first 8 or more characters: `Label print 1f6b353f`). The view and `./ise render` print the picture on it, projected along the part's thinnest direction and filling the part's extent; seen from the side a face looks out of, the picture's up is +Z on an upright face and +Y on a face looking up, so lay the label part out to match the artwork. Clear (transparent) pixels of a PNG show what is under the label: ink only, no film. Text you can draw yourself is better as `text()` ink or engraving; a printed picture is for artwork, fine print and symbols. `./ise look` shows the label part plain.
- `knurl({ radius, length, pitch, style })`; `thread({ diameter, length, internal, clearance })` for real ISO metric threads (printed nuts and bolts: clearance 0.1–0.2; keep mating threads a whole number of pitches apart, or set `phase`).
